Article 493 If an auction is concluded or a ruling is made in accordance with legal procedures to offset the debt with property, the ownership of the subject matter shall be transferred from the time the ruling on the auction conclusion or the ruling on the offset of debt is served on the buyer or the creditor who accepts the property in offset of the debt.

Article 494 If the subject matter of enforcement is a specific thing, the original thing shall be enforced. If the original thing is indeed damaged or destroyed, with the agreement of both parties, compensation may be made by converting the thing into a monetary value.
If the two parties cannot reach an agreement on the conversion for compensation, the People's Court shall terminate the enforcement procedure. The applicant for enforcement may initiate a separate action.

Article 495 If another person holds the property or negotiable instrument designated for delivery in the legal instrument, and after the People's Court issues a notice of assistance in enforcement in accordance with Articles 249(2) and (3) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, such person refuses to transfer the property or instrument, the People's Court may enforce by compulsory means and may also deal with the matter in accordance with Articles 114 and 115 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.
If the property or instrument is damaged or destroyed while held by another person, the matter shall be handled by reference to Article 494 of this Interpretation.
If another person claims that he lawfully holds the property or instrument, he may raise an enforcement objection in accordance with Article 227 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

Article 496 During enforcement, if the person subject to enforcement conceals property, accounting books, or other materials, the People's Court may, in addition to dealing with the matter in accordance with Article 111(1)(6) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, also order the person subject to enforcement to produce the concealed property, accounting books, or other materials. If the person subject to enforcement refuses to produce them, the People's Court may take search measures.
Article 497 The persons conducting the search shall dress in uniform as required and present the search warrant and their identification documents.

Article 498 When the People's Court conducts a search, it shall prohibit irrelevant persons from entering the search site; if the subject of the search is a citizen, it shall notify the person subject to enforcement or his adult family members and a person designated by the grassroots organization to be present; if the subject of the search is a legal person or any other organization, it shall notify the legal representative or the principal responsible person to be present. Their refusal to be present shall not affect the search.
A search of a female's body shall be conducted by female enforcement personnel.

Article 499 Where property that shall be subject to sealing-up or seizure pursuant to law is discovered during a search, the matter shall be handled in accordance with Article 245, paragraph 2 and Article 247 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

Article 500 A record of the search shall be prepared, which shall be signed, fingerprinted or sealed by the search personnel, the person searched, and other persons present. If any person refuses to sign, fingerprint, or seal, such fact shall be recorded in the search record.

Article 501 When the People's Court enforces a matured creditor's right owed by another person to the person subject to enforcement, it may make a ruling to freeze the creditor's right and notify such other person to perform to the applicant for enforcement.
If such other person raises an objection to the matured creditor's right, and the applicant for enforcement requests compulsory enforcement of the objected part, the People's Court shall not sustain such request. If an interested person raises an objection to the matured creditor's right, the People's Court shall handle the matter in accordance with Article 227 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.
If such other person denies a matured creditor's right confirmed by an effective legal instrument, the People's Court shall not sustain such denial.

Article 502 Where the People's Court needs to handle the procedures for the transfer of property right certificates, such as real estate certificates, land certificates, forest right certificates, patent certificates, trademark certificates, vehicle and vessel licenses, etc., during enforcement, it may handle such procedures in accordance with Article 251 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

Article 503 If a person subject to enforcement fails to perform an act obligation confirmed by an effective legal instrument, and such obligation may be performed by another person, the People's Court may select a substitute performer; if laws or administrative regulations impose qualification restrictions on the performance of such act obligation, the substitute performer shall be selected from among qualified persons. When necessary, the substitute performer may be determined through bidding.
The applicant for enforcement may recommend a substitute performer from among persons who meet the conditions, or may apply to perform the act by himself; whether to permit such application shall be decided by the People's Court.

Article 504 The amount of the substitute performance expenses shall be determined by the People's Court in light of the specific circumstances of the case, and shall be prepaid by the person subject to enforcement within a designated period. If the person subject to enforcement fails to prepay, the People's Court may enforce compulsory execution for such expenses.
After the substitute performance is completed, the person subject to enforcement may inspect and copy the expense list and the main vouchers.

Article 505 If the person subject to enforcement fails to perform an act specified in a legal instrument, and such act may only be performed by the person subject to enforcement, the People's Court may handle the matter in accordance with Article 111, paragraph 1, item (6) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.
If the person subject to enforcement still fails to perform within the performance period determined by the People's Court, the People's Court may handle the matter again in accordance with Article 111, paragraph 1, item (6) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

Article 506 If the person subject to enforcement delays performance, the interest during the period of delayed performance or the liquidated damages for delayed performance shall be calculated from the date on which the performance period specified in the judgment, ruling, or other legal instrument expires.

Article 507 If the person subject to enforcement fails to perform a non-monetary payment obligation within the period specified in a judgment, ruling, or other legal instrument, regardless of whether loss has been caused to the applicant for enforcement, the person subject to enforcement shall pay liquidated damages for delayed performance. If loss has been caused, the compensation shall be double the loss already suffered by the applicant for enforcement; if no loss has been caused, the liquidated damages for delayed performance may be determined by the People's Court according to the specific circumstances of the case.

Article 508 If the person subject to enforcement is a citizen or any other organization, after the commencement of the enforcement proceedings, any other creditor of the person subject to enforcement who has already obtained an enforcement basis may apply to the People's Court for participation in the distribution if such creditor discovers that the property of the person subject to enforcement is insufficient to satisfy all claims.
Any creditor who has a priority right or security interest in the property sealed up, seized, or frozen by the People's Court may directly apply for participation in the distribution and claim the right to be satisfied in priority.

Article 509 To apply for participation in distribution, the applicant shall submit a written application. The application shall state the facts and reasons for participating in the distribution and for the person subject to enforcement being unable to satisfy all claims, and shall be accompanied by the enforcement basis.
The application for participation in distribution shall be submitted after the commencement of the enforcement proceedings and before the completion of enforcement against the property of the person subject to enforcement.

Article 510 In the course of enforcement of participation in distribution, after deducting enforcement expenses from the proceeds obtained from enforcement and satisfying the claims entitled to priority of payment, ordinary claims shall, in principle, be satisfied in proportion to their respective amounts among all claims for which participation in distribution has been applied. For the remaining debts after satisfaction, the person subject to enforcement shall continue to satisfy them. If any creditor discovers that the person subject to enforcement has other property, such creditor may at any time request the People's Court to enforce.

Article 511 If multiple creditors apply for participation in distribution of the property subject to enforcement, the enforcing People's Court shall prepare a property distribution plan and serve it on each creditor and the person subject to enforcement. If any creditor or the person subject to enforcement raises an objection to the distribution plan, such objection shall be submitted in writing to the enforcing People's Court within fifteen days from the date of receipt of the distribution plan.

Article 512 If any creditor or the person subject to enforcement submits a written objection to the distribution plan, the enforcing People's Court shall notify the creditors and the person subject to enforcement who did not raise the objection.
If the creditors and the person subject to enforcement who did not raise the objection fail to raise any opposing opinion within fifteen days from the date of receipt of the notice, the enforcing People's Court shall review and revise the distribution plan in accordance with the objector's opinion and then distribute; if an opposing opinion is raised, the enforcing People's Court shall notify the objector. The objector may, within fifteen days from the date of receipt of the notice, file an action with the enforcing People's Court against the creditor or the person subject to enforcement who raised the opposing opinion; if the objector fails to file an action within the time limit, the enforcing People's Court shall distribute in accordance with the original distribution plan.
If distribution is made during the litigation period, the enforcing People's Court shall deposit an amount corresponding to the disputed claim.

Article 513 In the course of enforcement, if an enterprise legal person that serves as the person subject to enforcement falls within the circumstances specified in Article 2, paragraph 1 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law of the People's Republic of China, the enforcing People's Court shall, with the consent of one of the applicants for enforcement or the person subject to enforcement, rule to suspend the enforcement against such person subject to enforcement and transfer the relevant materials of the enforcement case to the People's Court at the domicile of the person subject to enforcement.

Article 514 The People's Court at the domicile of the person subject to enforcement shall, within thirty days from the date of receiving the relevant materials of the enforcement case, inform the enforcing People's Court of its ruling on whether to accept the bankruptcy case. If it decides not to accept the case, it shall return the relevant case materials to the enforcing People's Court.

Article 515 If the People's Court at the domicile of the person subject to enforcement rules to accept the bankruptcy case, the enforcing People's Court shall release the preservation measures against the property of the person subject to enforcement. If the People's Court at the domicile of the person subject to enforcement rules to declare the bankruptcy of the person subject to enforcement, the enforcing People's Court shall rule to terminate the enforcement against such person subject to enforcement.
If the People's Court at the domicile of the person subject to enforcement does not accept the bankruptcy case, the enforcing People's Court shall resume the enforcement.

Article 516 If the parties do not agree to the transfer of the bankruptcy case or the People's Court at the domicile of the person subject to enforcement does not accept the bankruptcy case, the enforcing People's Court shall, with respect to the property realized from enforcement, after deducting enforcement expenses and satisfying claims entitled to priority of payment, satisfy the ordinary claims in the order of the time when the property was sealed up, seized, or frozen during property preservation and enforcement.

Article 517 If a creditor requests the People's Court to continue enforcement in accordance with Article 254 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, such request shall not be subject to the limitation period for applying for enforcement as prescribed in Article 239 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

Article 518 If the person subject to enforcement fails to perform the obligations confirmed by a legal instrument, the People's Court may, in addition to imposing penalties on the person subject to enforcement, also include such person in the list of dishonest persons subject to enforcement according to the circumstances, and notify the information of the person subject to enforcement's non-performance or incomplete performance of obligations to his work unit, credit reference agencies, and other relevant institutions.

Article 519 If after investigation of property, no property available for enforcement is discovered, and if the applicant for enforcement signs to confirm or the enforcing People's Court forms a collegial panel to examine and verify and obtains approval from the president, the enforcing People's Court may rule to terminate the current enforcement proceedings.
After the enforcement is terminated in accordance with the preceding paragraph, if the applicant for enforcement discovers that the person subject to enforcement has property available for enforcement, the applicant may apply for enforcement again. A subsequent application shall not be subject to the limitation period for applying for enforcement.

Article 520 After enforcement is terminated due to withdrawal of the application, if a party applies for enforcement again within the limitation period for applying for enforcement as prescribed in Article 239 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the People's Court shall accept the application.

Article 521 Within six months after the conclusion of enforcement, if the person subject to enforcement or any other person commits an act of obstruction against the subject matter that has been enforced, the People's Court may, upon application, remove the obstruction, and may impose penalties in accordance with Article 111 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. If the act of obstruction causes loss to the enforcement creditor or any other person, the victim may bring a separate action.
XXII. Special Provisions on Procedures for Foreign-related Civil Actions

Article 523 A foreigner participating in litigation shall submit to the People's Court a passport or other identification document to prove his identity.
A foreign enterprise or organization participating in litigation shall have the identity certification documents submitted to the People's Court notarized by a notary institution in the country where it is located and authenticated by the embassy or consulate of the People's Republic of China in that country, or shall fulfill the certification procedures specified in the relevant treaty concluded between the People's Republic of China and that country.
A person representing a foreign enterprise or organization in litigation shall submit to the People's Court proof that he has the authority to participate in litigation as a representative, which proof shall be notarized by a notary institution in the country where it is located and authenticated by the embassy or consulate of the People's Republic of China in that country, or shall fulfill the certification procedures specified in the relevant treaty concluded between the People's Republic of China and that country.
The "country where it is located" referred to in this Article means the country where the foreign enterprise or organization is registered for establishment, or may also be a third country where the business registration procedures have been completed.

Article 524 Where notarization and authentication procedures are required in accordance with Article 264 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 523 of this Interpretation, and the country where the foreign party is located has no diplomatic relations with the People's Republic of China, the documents may be notarized by a notary institution of that country, authenticated by the embassy or consulate of a third country that has diplomatic relations with the People's Republic of China in that country, and then transmitted to the embassy or consulate of the People's Republic of China in that third country for authentication.

Article 525 If a foreigner, or a representative of a foreign enterprise or organization signs a power of attorney in the presence of a judge of the People's Court to appoint an agent to conduct civil litigation, the People's Court shall recognize such power of attorney.

Article 526 If a foreigner, or a representative of a foreign enterprise or organization signs a power of attorney within the territory of the People's Republic of China to appoint an agent to conduct civil litigation, and such power of attorney is notarized by a notarial institution of the People's Republic of China, the People's Court shall recognize such power of attorney.

Article 527 If the written materials submitted by a party to the People's Court are in a foreign language, the party shall simultaneously submit a Chinese translation to the People's Court.
If a party has objections to the Chinese translation, the parties shall jointly entrust a translation institution to provide a translated text; if the parties cannot reach an agreement on the choice of translation institution, the People's Court shall designate one.

Article 528 A foreign party in foreign-related civil litigation may appoint a national of his own country as a litigation agent, or may appoint a lawyer of his own country to act as a litigation agent in a non-lawyer capacity; an officer of a foreign embassy or consulate in China, when entrusted by a national of his own country, may act as a litigation agent in his personal capacity, but shall not enjoy diplomatic or consular privileges and immunities in the litigation.

Article 529 In foreign-related civil litigation, a foreign embassy or consulate in China may authorize an officer of its own mission, in the capacity of a diplomatic representative, to engage a lawyer of the People's Republic of China or a citizen of the People's Republic of China to represent its national who is a party and is not within the territory of the People's Republic of China in the civil litigation.

Article 530 In foreign-related civil litigation, if an agreement is reached through mediation by both parties, a mediation statement shall be prepared and issued. If a party requests the issuance of a judgment, a judgment may be prepared based on the content of the agreement and served on the parties.

Article 531 Parties to a foreign-related contract or other disputes over property rights and interests may, by written agreement, choose a foreign court at the place where the defendant has his domicile, the place of performance of the contract, the place of signing of the contract, the place where the plaintiff has his domicile, the location of the subject matter, the place where the tortious act is committed, or other places that have actual connection with the dispute to have jurisdiction.
For cases falling under the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of the People's Republic of China in accordance with Articles 33 and 266 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the parties may not by agreement choose a foreign court to have jurisdiction, except where an agreement to arbitrate is chosen.

Article 533 In a case over which both a court of the People's Republic of China and a foreign court have jurisdiction, if one party brings an action in a foreign court and the other party brings an action in a court of the People's Republic of China, the People's Court may accept the case. After a judgment is rendered, if the foreign court applies or a party requests the People's Court to recognize and enforce a judgment or ruling made by the foreign court in the case, such application or request shall not be granted, unless otherwise provided by an international treaty to which both countries are parties or have acceded.
If a judgment or ruling of a foreign court has already been recognized by the People's Court, and a party brings an action in the People's Court regarding the same dispute, the People's Court shall not accept the action.

Article 534 For a party who has no domicile within the territory of the People's Republic of China, if the litigation documents are served by public announcement and the party fails to appear for defense after the expiration of the announcement period, and the People's Court renders a default judgment, the People's Court shall still serve the judgment document by public announcement in accordance with Article 267, item (8) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. From the date when the public announcement of the judgment document expires for three months, if the party does not appeal within the thirty-day appeal period, the first-instance judgment shall take legal effect.

Article 535 If a foreigner, or a representative or principal responsible person of a foreign enterprise or organization is within the territory of the People's Republic of China, the People's Court may serve the documents on such natural person or the representative or principal responsible person of the foreign enterprise or organization.
The principal responsible person of a foreign enterprise or organization includes the directors, supervisors, senior officers, etc., of such enterprise or organization.

Article 536 If the country where the person to be served is located permits service by mail, the People's Court may serve by mail.
When serving by mail, an acknowledgment of service shall be enclosed. If the person to be served does not sign on the acknowledgment of service but signs on the mail receipt, it shall be deemed as service, and the date of signing shall be the date of service.
If, three months after the date of mailing, no proof of service is received, and it cannot be determined that service has been effected based on various circumstances, it shall be deemed that service by mail is not possible.

Article 537 If the People's Court serves litigation documents on a party by public announcement at the first instance, it may directly serve the litigation documents by public announcement at the second instance, except where the People's Court is able to serve by means other than public announcement.

Article 538 For a party who has a domicile within the territory of the People's Republic of China, the period for appeal against a judgment or ruling of the first-instance People's Court shall be governed by the period specified in Article 164 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China; for a party who has no domicile within the territory of the People's Republic of China, the period for appeal shall be governed by the period specified in Article 269 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. If the appeal periods for all parties have expired without any appeal, the judgment or ruling of the first-instance People's Court shall take legal effect.

Article 539 The period for the People's Court to examine an application for retrial filed by a party in a foreign-related civil case shall not be subject to the restrictions provided in Article 204 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

Article 540 An applicant who applies to the People's Court for enforcement of an award made by a foreign-related arbitration institution of the People's Republic of China shall submit a written application, together with the original award. If the applicant is a foreign party, the application shall be submitted in the Chinese language.

Article 541 When the People's Court enforces an arbitral award of a foreign-related arbitration institution by compulsory execution, if the person subject to enforcement raises a defense on the ground that there are circumstances specified in Article 274, paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the People's Court shall examine such defense and, based on the result of the examination, rule to enforce or not to enforce the award.

Article 542 Where, in accordance with Article 272 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, a foreign-related arbitration institution of the People's Republic of China submits a party's application for preservation to the People's Court for a ruling, the People's Court may examine the application and rule on whether to grant preservation. If it rules to grant preservation, it shall order the applicant to provide security; if the applicant fails to provide security, it shall rule to dismiss the application.
If a party applies for preservation of evidence, and the People's Court, after examination, considers that the provision of security is unnecessary, the applicant may not provide security.

Article 543 An applicant who applies to the People's Court for recognition and enforcement of a legally effective judgment or ruling made by a foreign court shall submit a written application, together with the original of the legally effective judgment or ruling made by the foreign court or a certified copy thereof, as well as a Chinese translation. If the foreign court's judgment or ruling is a default judgment or ruling, the applicant shall also submit the certification documents proving that the foreign court has legally summoned the party, except where the judgment or ruling has clearly stated such fact.
If an international treaty concluded or acceded to by the People's Republic of China has provisions on the documents to be submitted, the matter shall be handled in accordance with such provisions.

Article 544 If a party applies to an Intermediate People's Court of the People's Republic of China having jurisdiction for recognition and enforcement of a legally effective judgment or ruling made by a foreign court, and if the country where such court is located has not concluded or acceded to an international treaty with the People's Republic of China, nor has any reciprocal relationship, the People's Court shall rule to dismiss the application, except where a party applies to the People's Court for recognition of a legally effective divorce judgment made by a foreign court.
If the application for recognition and enforcement is dismissed by ruling, the party may bring an action in the People's Court.

Article 545 If a party applies to the People's Court for recognition and enforcement of an arbitral award made by an ad hoc arbitral tribunal outside the territory of the People's Republic of China, the People's Court shall handle the matter in accordance with Article 283 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

Article 546: Where a legally effective judgment or ruling made by a foreign court or a foreign arbitral award needs to be enforced by a people's court of the People's Republic of China, the party shall first apply to the people's court for recognition. After examination, the people's court shall, after making a ruling to recognize it, enforce it in accordance with the provisions of Book Three of the Civil Procedure Law.
Where a party only applies for recognition without simultaneously applying for enforcement, the people's court shall only examine whether recognition should be granted and make a ruling thereof.

Article 547: The period for a party to apply for recognition and enforcement of a legally effective judgment or ruling made by a foreign court or a foreign arbitral award shall be governed by the provisions of Article 239 of the Civil Procedure Law.
Where a party only applies for recognition without simultaneously applying for enforcement, the period for applying for enforcement shall be recalculated from the date on which the people's court's ruling on the recognition application takes effect.

Article 548: For a case involving the recognition and enforcement of a legally effective judgment or ruling made by a foreign court or a foreign arbitral award, the people's court shall form a collegiate panel for examination.
The people's court shall serve the application on the respondent. The respondent may present its opinions.
A ruling made by the people's court after examination shall take effect upon service.

Article 549: If a court of a country that has neither a judicial assistance treaty with the People's Republic of China nor a reciprocal relationship directly requests a people's court to provide judicial assistance without going through diplomatic channels, the people's court shall return the request and state the reasons.

Article 550: Where a party uses a judgment or ruling of a people's court of the People's Republic of China outside the territory of the People's Republic of China and requests the people's court of the People's Republic of China to certify its legal effect, or where a foreign court requests the people's court of the People's Republic of China to certify the legal effect of a judgment or ruling, the people's court that made the judgment or ruling may issue a certificate in the name of that court.

Article 551: When a people's court hears a civil action case involving the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, the Macao Special Administrative Region, or the Taiwan Region, it may refer to and apply the special provisions on civil procedure with foreign elements.
XXIII. Supplementary Provisions

Article 552: After this Interpretation is promulgated and comes into force, the Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China issued by the Supreme People's Court on July 14, 1992 shall be abolished simultaneously; any judicial interpretation previously issued by the Supreme People's Court that is inconsistent with this Interpretation shall cease to apply.
